label: Higher circulating monocyte count in more severe disease (with CD14 and CCL2 as supporting markers)
circularity: none (no monocyte variable in any label)
novelty_where: CCL2 by outcome published per cohort (CB517, CB017); CD14 by complicated status (CB112); monocyte activation proposed as a mechanism (CB107, CB119, CB517); CCL2 also published in an independent B. rossi cohort (CB037). No CB article combines independent sources, and the DS05 (Eastern Cape) monocyte association is unpublished. The sCD14/presepsin parallel is not made in a CB text found
sources: SRC-A, SRC-B, SRC-C, SRC-F (B. rossi); SRC-D (B. canis, transfer)
evidence: T02 B. rossi 4 of 4 sources in the expected direction, Stouffer one-sided p 4e-05, BH q 0.00016 over 8 themes (themes chosen after results were seen), leave-one-source-out max p 0.0105; with SRC-D 5 of 5
screen_reason: no single non-published source passes alone except SRC-F (DS05 monocytes with dullness, already seen); convergent across 4 B. rossi sources
refutation_reason: No single check rejects the lead. The DS05 monocyte-dullness association survives adjustment for haematocrit, total and differential leukocytes and illness days (partial rho about +0.28), and the post hoc marker choice was conservative. But the cross-source support outside the source that suggested it is weak: without SRC-F, Z 2.31, Bonferroni over 8 themes 0.084. In the two hard-outcome sources the monocyte difference is no larger than the WBC difference, and half of the DS07 CD14 signal goes with haemoglobin beta. Monocyte count does not track MCP-1, the CCL2 form is already published (CB107, CB517, CB037, CB017), and the only direct activation marker in B. rossi (CB504) points the other way in non-survivors.

label: Inflammation against regeneration at a given haematocrit (SV-09 residual axis 2) tracks dullness
circularity: none (habitus is not a laboratory label); partly restates leukocytes
novelty_where: inadequate regeneration and cytokine-suppressed erythropoiesis proposed in CB115, CB129, CB082, with the malaria parallel (CB129, CB115); no CB article links it to clinical severity
evidence: partial rho with habitus -0.26 (-0.40 to -0.10), p 0.003, family of 2 axes, n 140 (DS05, already seen: exploratory)
screen_reason: passes the statistical screen in one source; not replicable in other files (SV-09-02)
refutation_reason: The axis-2 association with habitus does not survive control for band neutrophils and monocytes (rho -0.10, -0.27 to +0.07), so it restates leukocytes already known to track dullness, a known driver under the spec. The named mechanism is also absent: at a given haematocrit the leukocyte and regeneration sides are uncorrelated (rho -0.002) and leukocytes do not go with lower ARC. What remains is a weak, uncorrected ARC-brighter link (rho +0.18, p 0.03) in one already-seen clinic file, which could be re-entered as a separate gap/test lead (the DS03-S-CB050 join) but not as K02.

label: Intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin, haem scavenging)
circularity: partial: DS07 label contains haematocrit < 0.15 and bilirubin > 30
novelty_where: SV-06a F1-01 measured_no_severity (CB082, CB412); haem oxygenase-1 never measured; haemopexin and haptoglobin measured without severity
evidence: T04: DS07 haemoglobin beta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), q 0.133; DS02 cfHb change high vs low dose +1.0 (exact p 0.2); Stouffer p 0.005, q 0.010, leave-one-source-out fails (max p 0.1), so not tier C
screen_reason: combined test passes but leave-one-source-out fails with 2 sources; gap lead by SV-06a
refutation_reason: The gap stands: no CB article relates measured cell-free haemoglobin or haem load to outcome in natural canine babesiosis, the human evidence (falciparum, knowlesi, sepsis) agrees, and canine assays exist. The programme's 'weak convergent support' does not hold. DS02 is a pure parasite-load effect that CB082 already reports. DS07 haemoglobin beta partly restates the label, cannot be put per unit of anaemia, moves with another red-cell protein (sample haemolysis not excluded), drops below significance when adjusted for lactoferrin or CD14 or when the top 3 dogs are removed, and has q 0.133. So T04 should be cited as a literature gap, not as a data signal.

label: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular traps (NETs, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin)
circularity: none for the released markers; bands are a known driver
novelty_where: SV-06a ranks 3, 4, 5, 9: never measured in canine babesiosis; band neutrophils and MPXI are published (CB050, CB040)
evidence: SV-08 neutrophil-granule score rose in 5 of 5 Beagles (also in mild dogs; MPO, ELANE missing); DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (-0.10 to +0.93), q 0.29; histone H4 untestable
screen_reason: gap lead by SV-06a; the existing data are within-dog changes or underpowered
refutation_reason: The gap is real: no study has measured NETs, cfDNA, nucleosomes, circulating histones, calprotectin or released MPO/elastase against severity or outcome in canine babesiosis, and CB107 states NETosis is unstudied. The canine support is weak and confounded: no signal passes correction (S100A8 q 0.29, H4 untestable), half the lactoferrin and a third of the S100A8 effect go with serum haemoglobin, the DS07 label contains band neutrophils, and SV-08 shows a response to infection with no severity gradient that tracks band counts. It remains a literature-driven gap lead, not a data-supported finding, and the human evidence itself is mixed.

label: Angiopoietin-2 and the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio
novelty_where: SV-06a rank 1, never measured in canine babesiosis
evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (6 human cohorts), validated canine assay
screen_reason: gap lead
refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured angiopoietin-2, the human severity evidence is strong (systematic review of 11 falciparum studies, sepsis meta-analysis of 33 studies) and a validated canine Ang-2 ELISA exists with prognostic data in canine sepsis. The candidate is weakened only because Ang-1 could not be measured with the validated kit, so the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio is not assayable in dogs; the lead should be restricted to Ang-2 and adjusted for haemolysis and creatinine.

label: VWF, ultra-large multimers and ADAMTS13
novelty_where: SV-06a rank 6, measured only against controls (CB446)
evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
screen_reason: gap lead
refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured VWF or ADAMTS13 against severity or outcome, and CB145, the obvious threat, measured factor activities but not VWF or ADAMTS13. Validated canine assays exist for both. The lead is weakened because the human VWF/ADAMTS13 ratio evidence rests largely on one small cohort and because the single canine measurement (CB446) found vWF activity lower, not higher, than in controls, so the direction of transfer cannot be assumed.

label: VEGF and soluble VEGFR-1 (sFlt-1)
novelty_where: SV-06a rank 2, never measured
evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine VEGF assay
screen_reason: gap lead
refutation_reason: The gap itself is real: no canine babesiosis study has measured VEGF or sFlt-1, and CB122 only names VEGF as an enriched pathway. But the tier D rule fails on the other two conditions at once. The human severity evidence is grade 2 at best and inconsistent in direction for VEGF (protective in cerebral malaria, raised in uncomplicated malaria, low with immunosuppression in human babesiosis), while the stronger sepsis sFlt-1 evidence rests on one cohort; and no canine sFlt-1 assay exists, so the half with the better human case cannot be measured in dogs at all.

label: Ferritin (hyperferritinaemia)
novelty_where: SV-06a rank 7, measured, no difference 7 vs 7 (CB242)
evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
screen_reason: gap lead
refutation_reason: Ferritin has never been measured against severity or outcome in canine babesiosis: the only measurement (CB242, 7 vs 7, infected versus healthy, no difference) has no severity contrast and no power, and CB132 is a single severe case with hyperferritinaemia. The human sepsis evidence is strong across three cohorts, and canine ferritin assays are in use. The lead is weakened because the malaria evidence is an infection contrast rather than a severity one, because no formal canine assay validation was found, and because ferritin in a haemolytic disease is heavily confounded by haemolysis and the acute-phase response.

label: Kynurenine pathway (kynurenine:tryptophan)
novelty_where: SV-06a rank 8, measured against controls in B. canis (CB091)
evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
screen_reason: gap lead
refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured the kynurenine pathway against severity or outcome; CB091 is an infected-versus-healthy contrast, which my re-analysis of its supplement confirms is large (Kyn/Trp delta +0.86, p 3.8e-04). The human sepsis and critical-illness evidence is strong across several cohorts and a validated canine plasma LC-MS/MS assay exists, so tier D holds. It is weakened because the nearest severity proxy that can be computed now, the CB071 renal-function groups, shows no urinary kynurenine or tryptophan difference, because the malaria evidence is mostly CSF and cerebral, and because kynurenine is confounded by azotaemia and by inflammatory intensity.
